current.text: Detroit got him in a trade from Oklahoma City.
He is projected as Detroit's sixth man and backup shooter. He is the first player off the bench, ahead of Ron Holland, Paul Reed and Daniss Jenkins.
Duncan Robinson is projected to start at shooting guard. Joe is the most likely player to challenge him for that starting spot.
He is valued around rank 250, outside the top 250 for fantasy. The expert sees him as a three-point streamer, not a player to draft.
Last season Detroit used a deep rotation of 12 to 13 players, which limited everyone's minutes.

durable.text: He is an elite three-point shooter with low usage who adds little else.
His fantasy value comes from threes, few turnovers and a good FT% on low volume. He is weak in rebounds, assists, steals and blocks.
His defense kept him off the floor in Oklahoma City's last two playoff runs, and he fell out of their playoff rotation. He does have some impact in forcing turnovers.
Detroit is built on defense. The front office wants only enough offense to get by.

note: Joe is not a draft target in our 144-player auction. Both Yahoo and ESPN value him at 0 USD, and his ranks of 258 on Yahoo and 190 on ESPN put him at or beyond the edge of the drafted pool. His projected 2.5 threes and 0.6 turnovers per game make him a short-term streamer for 3PM and TO, but he gives little in the other categories. Early in the season, check whether he takes the starting spot from Duncan Robinson or gets steady minutes in Detroit's deep rotation. A starting role would make him worth a waiver pickup.
